title: Opinions & discussions
goal: Give and ask for opinions, agree and disagree without offending anyone, say "it depends", "maybe" and "probably", argue a point about prices, politics or going abroad, and say what someone should have done.
intro:
Nepalis love a good argument — over tea, on a bus, in the comments under every news story. The topics are always the same: prices (**महँगी**), politicians (**नेता**), corruption (**भ्रष्टाचार**), Kathmandu's dust and traffic, and whether young people should go abroad. This unit gets you into those conversations.

The grammar is about **how sure you are** and **how hard you push**. You'll learn the 'maybe' words (**होला**, **हुन सक्छ**, **कि**), how to disagree softly (**मलाई त्यस्तो लाग्दैन** 'I don't think so', **त्यो त भर पर्छ** 'it depends'), and how to say what someone **should have** done: तिमीले पहिले नै **भन्नुपर्थ्यो**!

vocab.note: तिम्रो राय के छ? 'what's your take?'. Also विचार (unit 14).
यो विषयमा 'on this subject'. Also a school subject.
साँचो कुरा 'the truth'; साँचो भन्ने हो भने 'to tell the truth'.
X-मा भर पर्छ 'it depends on X'. Formal: निर्भर गर्छ.
म तिम्रो पक्षमा छु 'I'm on your side'.
X-को विरोध गर्नु 'to oppose / protest against X'.
Plural नेताहरू — usually said with a sigh.

vocab.en: rising prices, high cost of living

vocab.note: Plural युवाहरू. Also used as an adjective: युवा पुस्ता 'the young generation'.
बहस गर्नु 'to argue, debate'. A real fight is झगडा.
बकवास गर्नु 'to talk nonsense'. Blunt — friends only.
आफ्नो कुरामा अड्नु 'to stick to your guns'.

vocab.en: to persuade, talk round; to make up with

phrases.native: साँचो भन्ने हो भने, मलाई मन परेन।
phrases.roman: sāṃcho bhanne ho bhane, malāi man parena.
phrases.en: To be honest, I didn't like it.

phrases.native: कुरा त ठीक हो, तर अलि गाह्रो छ।
phrases.roman: kurā ta ṭhik ho, tara ali gāhro chha.
phrases.en: You've got a point, but it's not that easy.
After all, everyone's entitled to their opinion.
You should have said so earlier!

phrases.native: एक मिनेट, मेरो कुरा त सुन न!
phrases.roman: ek mineṭ, mero kurā ta suna na!
phrases.en: Hang on — at least hear me out!

grammar.title: Maybe, probably, might: होला, -न सक्छ, कि
grammar.body:
Nepali has a whole scale of 'how sure am I?'. From least to most certain:

**कि** at the end of a question — 'maybe…?', a tentative guess: ऊ बिरामी छ **कि**? 'is he ill, maybe?'
**सायद** 'perhaps' (unit 14), usually with a -ला verb: **सायद** ऊ आउ**ला** 'perhaps he'll come'.
**-न सक्छ** 'might, could' (possibility — the same सक्नु as 'can'): पानी **पर्न सक्छ** 'it might rain' · ऊ ढिलो **आउन सक्छ**. On its own: **हुन सक्छ** 'could be'.
**होला** 'probably is' and the **-ला** future (unit 17) — a guess you're fairly confident about: ऊ अफिसमा **होला** · ऊ सुतेको **होला** 'he's probably asleep'. Negative: **होइन होला / छैन होला** 'probably not'.
**पक्कै / पक्का / निश्चित** — sure.

**Guessing about the past**: -एको + **होला**: उनीहरू पुगिसके**का होलान्** 'they've probably arrived by now', ऊ घर गएको होला 'he's probably gone home'.

**The trap**: -न सक्छ is both 'can' and 'might'. Context decides: म आउन सक्छु 'I can come' vs ऊ आउन सक्छ 'he might come'. If you mean 'maybe', adding **होला** or **सायद** makes it clear.

examples.en: There might be a power cut today.

grammar.title: Disagreeing gently: मलाई त्यस्तो लाग्दैन
grammar.body:
**I don't think…** — as in English, the 'not' goes on 'think', not on the idea: X **जस्तो मलाई लाग्दैन** 'I don't think X'. ऊ आउँछ जस्तो मलाई **लाग्दैन** 'I don't think he's coming'. Because लाग्नु is an experiencer verb (मलाई…), it stays in the 'it' form: **लाग्दैन**, never लाग्दिनँ. Short version: **मलाई त्यस्तो लाग्दैन** 'I don't think so'.

**Softening** — Nepalis rarely say a flat 'you're wrong' (**तिमी गलत छौ** sounds rude). Instead:
• **कुरा त ठीक हो, तर…** 'that's true, but…'
• **हो होला, तर…** 'you may be right, but…'
• **मेरो विचारमा…** 'in my view…' · **साँचो भन्ने हो भने…** 'to be honest…'
• **त्यो त भर पर्छ** 'it depends' — X-**मा भर पर्छ** 'it depends on X': पैसामा भर पर्छ.

**Agreeing**: **त्यही त!** 'exactly!' · **ठीक भन्यौ** 'you're right' · **म पनि त्यही भन्छु** 'that's what I say too'.

**With elders** don't contradict at all directly: start with **हजुर, तर…** or **हो होला, तर…** and frame your view as a question.

examples.native: यो काम एक दिनमा सकिन्छ जस्तो मलाई लाग्दैन।
examples.roman: yo kām ek dinmā sakinchha jasto malāi lāgdaina.
examples.en: I don't think this job can be finished in a day.

examples.native: मलाई त्यस्तो लाग्दैन, तर तिमीलाई जे ठीक लाग्छ गर।
examples.roman: malāi tyasto lāgdaina, tara timilāi je ṭhik lāgchha gara.
examples.en: I don't think so, but do whatever you think is right.

examples.native: हो होला, तर मेरो विचार अलि अर्कै छ।
examples.roman: ho holā, tara mero bichār ali arkai chha.
examples.en: You may be right, but I see it a bit differently.

examples.native: त्यही त! म पनि त्यही भन्छु।
examples.roman: tyahi ta! ma pani tyahi bhanchhu.
examples.en: Exactly! That's what I say too.

grammar.title: Should, should have: -नुपर्छ, -नुपर्थ्यो
grammar.body:
**Should / must** (unit 15): verb-**नुपर्छ**: सरकारले केही **गर्नुपर्छ** 'the government should do something'.

**Should have / was supposed to**: verb-**नुपर्थ्यो** — the same pattern with the past of पर्नु. It doesn't change for the person; the doer of a transitive verb takes **ले**:
तिमीले पहिले नै **भन्नुपर्थ्यो** 'you should have said so earlier'
हामी अलि चाँडो **निस्कनुपर्थ्यो** 'we should have left a bit earlier'

**Shouldn't have**: verb-**नुहुँदैनथ्यो** (from -नुहुँदैन 'mustn't', unit 9): मैले त्यसो **भन्नुहुँदैनथ्यो** 'I shouldn't have said that'.

A slightly fuller form, **-नुपर्ने थियो**, means the same and is common too — unit 36 uses it for regrets and 'if only'.

**The trap**: **-नुपर्‍यो** (unit 15) is 'had to — and did': मैले अफिस जानुपर्‍यो 'I had to go to the office'. **-नुपर्थ्यो** is 'should have (but didn't)' — or, about the past in general, 'used to have to': सानो छँदा दिनहुँ पानी बोक्नुपर्थ्यो 'when I was little I had to carry water every day'.

examples.native: मैले पहिले नै टिकट बुक गर्नुपर्थ्यो।
examples.roman: maile pahile nai ṭikaṭ buk garnuparthyo.
examples.en: I should have booked the ticket earlier.
You shouldn't have said that to him.

examples.native: सरकारले यो सडक पोहोर नै बनाउनुपर्थ्यो।
examples.roman: sarkārle yo saḍak pohor nai banāunuparthyo.
examples.en: The government should have built this road last year.

examples.native: हामी अलि चाँडो निस्कनुपर्थ्यो, जाममा पर्‍यौँ।
examples.roman: hāmi ali chāṃḍo niskanuparthyo, jāmmā paryauṃ.
examples.en: We should have left earlier — we got stuck in traffic.
When I was little I had to carry water every day.

dialogue.title: Korea or Kathmandu?
dialogue.setting: Bibek, Sarah and Suman over tea at a Kathmandu tea shop. Suman is thinking of going back to work in Korea.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: सुमन, फेरि कोरिया जाने रे, साँच्चै हो?
lines.roman: Suman, pheri Koriyā jāne re, sāṃchchai ho?
lines.en: Suman, I hear you're going back to Korea — is it true?

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: हुन सक्छ। यहाँ के छ र? काम छैन, महँगी उस्तै।
lines.roman: huna sakchha. yahāṃ ke chha ra? kām chhaina, mahaṃgi ustai.
lines.en: Could be. What is there here? No work, and prices as bad as ever.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: मलाई त्यस्तो लाग्दैन। मेहनत गरे यहाँ पनि केही गर्न सकिन्छ।
lines.roman: malāi tyasto lāgdaina. mehanat gare yahāṃ pani kehi garna sakinchha.
lines.en: I don't think so. If you work hard you can make something of yourself here too.

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: कुरा त ठीक हो, तर तलब हेर न! कोरियामा एक महिनामा जति कमाउँछु, यहाँ छ महिनामा पनि कमाउँदिनँ।
lines.roman: kurā ta ṭhik ho, tara talab hera na! Koriyāmā ek mahināmā jati kamāuṃchhu, yahāṃ chha mahināmā pani kamāuṃdinaṃ.
lines.en: That's true, but look at the salaries! What I earn in a month in Korea I wouldn't earn in six months here.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: तर परिवार नि? तिम्री आमा के भन्नुहुन्छ?
lines.roman: tara pariwār ni? timri āmā ke bhannuhunchha?
lines.en: But what about your family? What does your mum say?

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: आमा त रुनुहुन्छ। तर आखिर पैसा पनि त चाहियो नि।
lines.roman: āmā ta runuhunchha. tara ākhir paisā pani ta chāhiyo ni.
lines.en: Mum cries, of course. But after all, you need money too.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: साँचो भन्ने हो भने, सरकारले युवाको लागि केही गर्नुपर्थ्यो।
lines.roman: sāṃcho bhanne ho bhane, sarkārle yuwāko lāgi kehi garnuparthyo.
lines.en: To be honest, the government should have done something for young people.

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: त्यही त! नेताहरू आफ्नै कुरामा मस्त छन्।
lines.roman: tyahi ta! netāharu āphnai kurāmā mast chhan.
lines.en: Exactly! The politicians are wrapped up in their own affairs.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: त्यो त भर पर्छ। मेरो विचारमा, दुई-तीन वर्ष गएर, सीप सिकेर फर्कनु ठीक होला।
lines.roman: tyo ta bhar parchha. mero bichārmā, dui-tin barsa gaera, sip sikera pharkanu ṭhik holā.
lines.en: Well, it depends. I think going for two or three years, learning some skills and coming back might be OK.

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: हो, त्यो चाहिँ ठीक हो। तर फर्केर आउनैपर्छ है!
lines.roman: ho, tyo chāhiṃ ṭhik ho. tara pharkera āunaiparchha hai!
lines.en: Yes, that I can agree with. But you HAVE to come back, OK!

lines.speaker: Suman
lines.native: पक्का आउँछु। अब बहस पुग्यो, चिया सेलायो!
lines.roman: pakkā āuṃchhu. aba bahas pugyo, chiyā selāyo!
lines.en: I'll definitely come back. Enough arguing — the tea's gone cold!

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.en: Right — the next round of tea is on me!

culture:
Political talk is everywhere in Nepal — at the **चिया पसल** (tea shop), on long bus rides, in family courtyards — and it's mostly good-humoured: everyone agrees the **नेताहरू** are the problem, and the fun is in arguing about the details. Debates among friends get loud, but **बकवास!** and **के बकवास गरेको!** are teasing, not insults. Everyone has an opinion on **foreign employment**: hundreds of thousands of Nepalis leave each year for the Gulf, Malaysia, Korea and Japan, and money sent home makes up roughly a quarter of the economy, so 'should young people go abroad?' is the national debate.

With people older than you, disagree by asking rather than telling: **हजुर, तर यस्तो पनि त हुन सक्छ नि?** 'yes, but couldn't it also be like this?'. Topics that can turn sensitive with people you don't know well are caste, religion, the monarchy and India–Nepal relations — listen first. Ending an argument gracefully is an art: **आखिर सबैको आफ्नो राय हुन्छ** or simply ordering another round of tea.

lessons.title: What do you think?

tip.title: Asking for and giving opinions
tip.body:
- Ask: **तिम्रो राय के छ?** · तपाईं**लाई** के लाग्छ?
- Give: **मेरो विचारमा** … · **मलाई लाग्छ**, …
- Be frank: **साँचो भन्ने हो भने** 'to be honest'.
- 'Think' is an experiencer verb: **मलाई / तिमीलाई** लाग्छ — not मैले, not तिमीले.

new: साँचो भन्ने हो भने, मलाई मन परेन।

sentences.native: यो विषयमा तपाईंको राय के छ?
sentences.roman: yo bisaymā tapāiṃko rāy ke chha?
sentences.en: What's your opinion on this?

sentences.native: मेरो विचारमा, यो राम्रो निर्णय हो।
sentences.roman: mero bichārmā, yo rāmro nirnaya ho.
sentences.en: In my opinion, it's a good decision.

sentences.native: मलाई लाग्छ, उसको तर्क ठीक छ।
sentences.roman: malāi lāgchha, usko tarka ṭhik chha.
sentences.en: I think his argument makes sense.

sentences.native: तिमीलाई के लाग्छ, किन यस्तो भयो?
sentences.roman: timilāi ke lāgchha, kina yasto bhayo?
sentences.en: What do you think — why did this happen?

sentences.native: यसको कारण के होला?
sentences.roman: yasko kāran ke holā?
sentences.en: What could be the reason for this?

sentences.native: एउटा उदाहरण दिऊँ?
sentences.roman: euṭā udāharan diuṃ?
sentences.en: Shall I give you an example?

sentences.native: साँचो भन्ने हो भने, मलाई यो प्लान राम्रो लागेन।
sentences.roman: sāṃcho bhanne ho bhane, malāi yo plān rāmro lāgena.
sentences.en: To be honest, I don't think much of this plan.

sentences.native: तपाईंलाई के लाग्छ, म के गरूँ?
sentences.roman: tapāiṃlāi ke lāgchha, ma ke garuṃ?
sentences.en: What do you think — what should I do?

sentences.native: उसले राम्रो तर्क दियो, तर म सहमत छैनँ।
sentences.roman: usle rāmro tarka diyo, tara ma sahamat chhainaṃ.
sentences.en: He made a good point, but I don't agree.

sentences.native: साँचो कुरा भन, तिमीलाई मन पर्‍यो कि परेन?
sentences.roman: sāṃcho kurā bhana, timilāi man paryo ki parena?
sentences.en: Tell me the truth — did you like it or not?

tip.title: How sure are you?
tip.body:
- **कि?** 'maybe?': सन्चो छैन **कि**?
- **-न सक्छ** 'might': पानी **पर्न सक्छ**. On its own: **हुन सक्छ** 'could be'.
- **होला** 'probably': अफिसमा **होला**, सुतेको **होला**. Not: **होइन होला**.
- **सायद** + -ला: सायद ऊ आउ**ला**.

sentences.native: आज पानी पर्न सक्छ, छाता लैजाऊ।
sentences.roman: āja pāni parna sakchha, chhātā laijāu.
sentences.en: It might rain today — take an umbrella.

sentences.native: दिदी अहिले अफिसमा हुनुहुन्छ होला।
sentences.roman: didi ahile aphismā hunuhunchha holā.
sentences.en: My sister's probably at the office now.

sentences.native: उसले फोन उठाएन, सुतेको होला।
sentences.roman: usle phon uṭhāena, suteko holā.
sentences.en: He didn't pick up — he's probably asleep.

sentences.native: भोलि बन्द हुन सक्छ रे।
sentences.roman: bholi banda huna sakchha re.
sentences.en: Apparently there might be a strike tomorrow.

sentences.native: सायद ऊ आउला, सायद नआउला।
sentences.roman: sāyad u āulā, sāyad naāulā.
sentences.en: Maybe he'll come, maybe he won't.

sentences.native: यो कुरा निश्चित छैन, हल्ला मात्र हो।
sentences.roman: yo kurā nischit chhaina, hallā mātra ho.
sentences.en: This isn't certain — it's just a rumour.

sentences.native: तिमीलाई सन्चो छैन कि?
sentences.roman: timilāi sancho chhaina ki?
sentences.en: Are you not feeling well, maybe?

sentences.native: यो पसल आज खुला होला कि?
sentences.roman: yo pasal āja khulā holā ki?
sentences.en: Do you think this shop might be open today?

sentences.native: उनीहरू ढिलो आउन सक्छन्, पर्खौँ।
sentences.roman: uniharu ḍhilo āuna sakchhan, parkhauṃ.
sentences.en: They might be late — let's wait.

sentences.native: पक्का होइन, तर उनीहरू बिहे गर्दै छन् होला।
sentences.roman: pakkā hoina, tara uniharu bihe gardai chhan holā.
sentences.en: I'm not sure, but they're probably getting married.

lessons.title: I don't think so — disagreeing nicely

tip.title: I don't think…: … जस्तो लाग्दैन
tip.body:
- Put 'not' on **think**: ऊ आउँछ जस्तो **लाग्दैन** 'I don't think he's coming' — not ऊ आउँदैन जस्तो लाग्छ.
- It's always the 'it' form: **लाग्दैन**, never लाग्दिनँ.
- Soften: **कुरा त ठीक हो, तर…** · **हो होला, तर…**
- 'It depends on X': X-**मा भर पर्छ**.
tip.pattern: X + जस्तो (मलाई) लाग्दैन  ·  X-मा भर पर्छ

new: कुरा त ठीक हो, तर अलि गाह्रो छ।

sentences.native: ऊ आज आउँछ जस्तो लाग्दैन।
sentences.roman: u āja āuṃchha jasto lāgdaina.
sentences.en: I don't think he's coming today.

sentences.native: मलाई त यो प्लान ठीक लाग्दैन।
sentences.roman: malāi ta yo plān ṭhik lāgdaina.
sentences.en: I don't think this plan is right.

sentences.native: उसको कुरा सही हो जस्तो मलाई लाग्दैन।
sentences.roman: usko kurā sahi ho jasto malāi lāgdaina.
sentences.en: I don't think what he says is true.

sentences.native: त्यो त कति पैसा छ भन्नेमा भर पर्छ।
sentences.roman: tyo ta kati paisā chha bhannemā bhar parchha.
sentences.en: That depends on how much money there is.

sentences.native: मौसममा भर पर्छ, पानी पर्‍यो भने जाँदैनौँ।
sentences.roman: mausammā bhar parchha, pāni paryo bhane jāṃdainauṃ.
sentences.en: It depends on the weather — if it rains we won't go.

sentences.native: म यो नियमको विरोध गर्छु।
sentences.roman: ma yo niyamko birodh garchhu.
sentences.en: I'm against this rule.

sentences.native: धेरै मान्छेले उहाँलाई समर्थन गर्छन्।
sentences.roman: dherai mānchhele uhāṃlāi samarthan garchhan.
sentences.en: Lots of people support him.

sentences.native: तिमी कसको पक्षमा छौ?
sentences.roman: timi kasko pakchhamā chhau?
sentences.en: Whose side are you on?

sentences.native: कुरा त ठीक हो, तर सबैलाई त्यस्तो लाग्दैन।
sentences.roman: kurā ta ṭhik ho, tara sabailāi tyasto lāgdaina.
sentences.en: That's true, but not everyone sees it that way.

sentences.native: पहिले मलाई पनि त्यस्तै लागेको थियो।
sentences.roman: pahile malāi pani tyastai lāgeko thiyo.
sentences.en: I used to think the same at first.

tip.title: Should and should have
tip.body:
- **Should** (now, in general): verb-**नुपर्छ**: सरकारले केही **गर्नुपर्छ**.
- **Should have**: verb-**नुपर्थ्यो**: पहिले नै **गर्नुपर्थ्यो**.
- **Shouldn't have**: verb-**नुहुँदैनथ्यो**.
- The doer of a transitive verb takes **ले**: नेताहरू**ले**.

sentences.native: अब सरकारले महँगी घटाउनुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: aba sarkārle mahaṃgi ghaṭāunuparchha.
sentences.en: The government should bring prices down now.

sentences.native: नेताहरूले यो काम दस वर्ष पहिले नै गर्नुपर्थ्यो।
sentences.roman: netāharule yo kām das barsa pahile nai garnuparthyo.
sentences.en: The politicians should have done this ten years ago.

sentences.native: सरकारले भ्रष्टाचार रोक्नुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: sarkārle bhrasṭāchār roknuparchha.
sentences.en: The government has to stop corruption.

sentences.native: भोट हाल्न सबै जानुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: bhoṭ hālna sabai jānuparchha.
sentences.en: Everyone should go and vote.

sentences.native: पोहोर मैले भोट हाल्न जानुपर्थ्यो, तर गइनँ।
sentences.roman: pohor maile bhoṭ hālna jānuparthyo, tara gainaṃ.
sentences.en: Last year I should have gone to vote, but I didn't.

sentences.native: काठमाडौंमा जाडोमा प्रदूषण साह्रै धेरै हुन्छ।
sentences.roman: kāṭhmāḍauṃmā jāḍomā pradusan sāhrai dherai hunchha.
sentences.en: In Kathmandu the pollution gets really bad in winter.

sentences.native: बेरोजगारीले गर्दा धेरै मान्छे विदेश जान्छन्।
sentences.roman: berojgārile gardā dherai mānchhe bides jānchhan.
sentences.en: Because of unemployment lots of people go abroad.

sentences.native: यो मुद्दामा सरकारले पहिले नै बोल्नुपर्थ्यो।
sentences.roman: yo muddāmā sarkārle pahile nai bolnuparthyo.
sentences.en: The government should have spoken out on this issue earlier.

sentences.native: नेताहरूले त्यस्तो भन्नुहुँदैनथ्यो।
sentences.roman: netāharule tyasto bhannuhuṃdainathyo.
sentences.en: The politicians shouldn't have said that.

sentences.native: अचेल सबै कुरा महँगो भयो, तलबले पुग्दैन।
sentences.roman: achel sabai kurā mahaṃgo bhayo, talabale pugdaina.
sentences.en: Everything's got expensive these days — salaries don't stretch.

sentences.native: अचेल धेरै युवा पढ्न विदेश जान्छन्।
sentences.roman: achel dherai yuwā paḍhna bides jānchhan.
sentences.en: These days lots of young people go abroad to study.

sentences.native: विदेश जानुको फाइदा पनि छ, नोक्सान पनि छ।
sentences.roman: bides jānuko phāidā pani chha, noksān pani chha.
sentences.en: Going abroad has its pros and its cons.

sentences.native: हाम्रो पुस्ताका धेरै साथी विदेशमा छन्।
sentences.roman: hāmro pustākā dherai sāthi bidesmā chhan.
sentences.en: Lots of friends from our generation are abroad.

sentences.native: यहीँ बसेर काम गर्दा के फाइदा?
sentences.roman: yahiṃ basera kām gardā ke phāidā?
sentences.en: What's the point of staying here and working?

sentences.native: फाइदा त छ नि, परिवारसँगै बस्न पाइन्छ।
sentences.roman: phāidā ta chha ni, pariwārsaṃgai basna pāinchha.
sentences.en: Of course there's a point — you get to live with your family.

sentences.native: आखिर यो आफ्नै देश हो।
sentences.roman: ākhir yo āphnai des ho.
sentences.en: After all, it's our own country.

sentences.native: विदेश गएर नोक्सान भयो भने के गर्ने?
sentences.roman: bides gaera noksān bhayo bhane ke garne?
sentences.en: And what if you go abroad and lose out?

sentences.native: सायद युवाहरू फर्केर आउलान्।
sentences.roman: sāyad yuwāharu pharkera āulān.
sentences.en: Maybe the young people will come back.

sentences.native: आखिर निर्णय तिम्रो हो।
sentences.roman: ākhir nirnaya timro ho.
sentences.en: In the end it's your decision.

sentences.native: मेरो विचारमा, नयाँ पुस्ताले यहीँ केही गर्न सक्छ।
sentences.roman: mero bichārmā, nayāṃ pustāle yahiṃ kehi garna sakchha.
sentences.en: In my view, the new generation can make something happen here.

lessons.title: Arguing — and making up

tip.title: You should have…! I shouldn't have…
tip.body:
- Blame: तिमीले **भन्नुपर्थ्यो** 'you should have said'.
- Own up: मैले त्यसो **भन्नुहुँदैनथ्यो**, माफ गर 'I shouldn't have said that, sorry'.
- Don't mix up **-नुपर्‍यो** 'had to (and did)' with **-नुपर्थ्यो** 'should have (but didn't)'.

new: एक मिनेट, मेरो कुरा त सुन न!

sentences.native: तिमीले मलाई पहिले नै सोध्नुपर्थ्यो।
sentences.roman: timile malāi pahile nai sodhnuparthyo.
sentences.en: You should have asked me first.

sentences.native: मैले त्यसो भन्नुहुँदैनथ्यो, माफ गर।
sentences.roman: maile tyaso bhannuhuṃdainathyo, māph gara.
sentences.en: I shouldn't have said that — sorry.

sentences.native: मैले उसलाई मनाउन धेरै कोसिस गरेँ।
sentences.roman: maile uslāi manāuna dherai kosis gareṃ.
sentences.en: I tried really hard to talk him round.

sentences.native: हामीले यो बहस सुरु नै गर्नुहुँदैनथ्यो।
sentences.roman: hāmile yo bahas suru nai garnuhuṃdainathyo.
sentences.en: We should never have started this argument.

sentences.native: हामीले टिकट पहिले नै किन्नुपर्थ्यो, अब सकियो।
sentences.roman: hāmile ṭikaṭ pahile nai kinnuparthyo, aba sakiyo.
sentences.en: We should have bought the tickets earlier — now they're sold out.

sentences.native: ऊ बकवास गर्छ, उसको कुरा नसुन।
sentences.roman: u bakwās garchha, usko kurā nasuna.
sentences.en: He talks rubbish — don't listen to him.

sentences.native: तिमीले मलाई फोन गर्नुपर्थ्यो नि!
sentences.roman: timile malāi phon garnuparthyo ni!
sentences.en: You should have called me!

sentences.native: हामीले अलि बिस्तारै कुरा गर्नुपर्थ्यो।
sentences.roman: hāmile ali bistārai kurā garnuparthyo.
sentences.en: We should have talked a bit more calmly.

sentences.native: तिमीले पहिले नै मेरो कुरा मान्नुपर्थ्यो!
sentences.roman: timile pahile nai mero kurā mānnuparthyo!
sentences.en: You should have listened to me in the first place!

sentences.native: उसलाई मनाउन गाह्रो छ, ऊ आफ्नो कुरामा अड्छ।
sentences.roman: uslāi manāuna gāhro chha, u āphno kurāmā aḍchha.
sentences.en: He's hard to persuade — he sticks to his guns.
